title: Review stringency — classified findings, per-level outcomes and a debt register
summary: Grounds the decision on how strict review should be. A 14-day record of 5,971 findings on 869 PRs shows one bar for everything: missing tests top the list (794) and cost the most fix rounds, about a third of ruled findings were not real, and the auto-block policy overrode a reviewer not-real 126 times, while no security finding stalled delivery. Outside models (ASVS levels, CVSS environmental scoring, SRE error budgets, SQALE, the Fowler debt quadrant, new-code quality gates, AI-code failure modes) support a table of class by release level with four outcomes: block, expedite, debt, advisory.
